claim: Representation collapse between experts is a first-order failure mode of sparse-MoE training: experts converge to near-identical representations, which harms model performance and causes parameter redundancy even when FLOPs per token are held constant.
stance_target: the repo's treatment of expert collapse / load balancing as a risk that makes MoE experiments non-trivial at small scale
scope_conditions: Sparse mixture-of-experts LLMs; abstract-level claim from Findings of NAACL 2025
quoted_support: Regardless of several notable successes of SMoE, effective training such architecture remains elusive due to the representation collapse problem, which in turn harms model performance and causes parameter redundancy.

claim: SimSMoE claims a similarity-based routing algorithm that guarantees a solution to expert representation collapse under a fixed FLOPs budget, i.e. the fix is claimed to be free in compute terms.
stance_target: whether MoE routing fixes can be adopted without changing the compute budget on a fixed-FLOPs box
scope_conditions: Fixed FLOPs budget; guarantee stated in the abstract, not verified here (landing page only)
quoted_support: we present Similarity-based Sparse Mixture of Experts (SimSMoE), a novel similarity of neural network algorithm, that guarantees a solution to address the representation collapse issue between experts given a fixed FLOPs budget.

claim: The method is evaluated on three large language models for both pre-training and fine-tuning, and outperforms other SMoE routing policies — but this note is the ACL Anthology metadata page only, so no numbers, model sizes or training costs are available from it.
stance_target: the evidence weight this source can carry
scope_conditions: ACL Anthology landing page (abstract + BibTeX), ~1.1k words; primary PDF at aclanthology.org/2025.findings-naacl.107.pdf
quoted_support: We conduct extensive empirical evaluations on three large language models for both Pre-training and Fine-tuning tasks to illustrate the efficacy, robustness, and scalability of our method.
